creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers (Hugging Face, cohere.ai)
description: STS22 is a crosslingual semantic textual similarity dataset containing sentence pairs across 18 language pairs (among Arabic, English, French, German, Turkish, Spanish, Polish, Italian, Russian and Chinese). The goal is to assess the similarity of two sentences in different languages, with continuous similarity scores from 0 to 5. It is part of the MTEB benchmark's STS task.
inLanguage: ar, en, fr, de, tr, es, pl, it, ru, zh
name: STS22
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentence pairs are annotated with continuous similarity scores from 0 to 5, with higher numbers indicating more similar sentences. Spearman correlation based on cosine similarity serves as the main evaluation metric.
rai:dataCollection: STS22 is part of the SemEval STS benchmark series. It contains crosslingual sentence pairs with similarity scores from 0 to 5. The selection of sentences includes text from image captions, news headlines and user forums, covering 18 language pairs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentence pairs drawn from image captions, news headlines and user forums, covering crosslingual pairs across 18 language pairs.
rai:dataLimitations: MTEB's multilingual coverage is limited: retrieval and clustering tasks are English-only. STS22 is included as a multilingual STS dataset but the benchmark overall lacks multilingual retrieval and clustering datasets.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB (including STS22) aims to provide reliable embedding performance estimates across languages, enabling better selection of multilingual text embedding models for real-world applications such as search, clustering, and text mining.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating text embedding models on crosslingual semantic textual similarity tasks; benchmarking multilingual embedding models as part of the MTEB benchmark.

evidence.rai:dataCollection: STS12, STS13, STS14, STS15, STS16, STS17, STS22, STSBenchmark (Agirre et al., 2012, 2013) Original STS benchmark, with scores from 0 to 5. The selection of sentences includes text from image captions, news headlines and user forums. In total they contain between 1,000 and 20,000 sentences.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The selection of sentences includes text from image captions, news headlines and user forums. In total they contain between 1,000 and 20,000 sentences. STS12 - STS16 and STSBenchmark are monolingual english benchmarks. STS17 and STS22 contain crosslingual pairs of sentences.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and thus serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are continuous scores with higher numbers indicating more similar sentences. The provided model is used to embed the sentences and their similarity is computed using various distance metrics. Distances are benchmarked with ground truth similarities using Pearson and Spearman correlations. Spearman correlation based on cosine similarity serves as the main metric.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: MTEB contains multilingual classification, STS and bitext mining datasets. However, retrieval and clustering are English-only. SGPT-BLOOM-7B1-msmarco is geared towards multilingual retrieval datasets and due to the lack thereof cannot be comprehensively benchmarked in MTEB.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and thus serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks. MTEB consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks.
evidence.datePublished: MTEB incorporates SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR alongside a variety of other datasets from various tasks to provide a holistic performance review of text embedding models.
evidence.isLiveDataset: Through versioning at a dataset and software level, we aim to make it easy to reproduce results in MTEB. JSON files corresponding to all results available in this paper have been made available together with the MTEB benchmark.
